scope: Representative Green Line B surface service along the existing BU Commonwealth Avenue median. This is campus scenery, not a real-time transit service or a reconstruction of every current work-zone change.

sources.supports: Existing stop identifiers, names, latitude and longitude: Blandford Street, Boston University East, Boston University Central, Amory Street and Babcock Street. The cached route's downtown end is Government Center.
sources.reviewLimit: The live website/API could not be reread through the web tool during this pass. Existing cached official records are retained; no new live timetable, temporary closure or route-terminal claim is made.

sources.supports: Amory and Babcock replaced the former four-stop West Campus arrangement in November 2021. Official university photograph of an eastbound green trolley at Amory and article describe the longer, accessible platforms, canopies, lighting and signs.
Existing modern station design references: 225-foot platforms and 150-foot canopies; unchanged in this implementation.

CAF confirms that 24 Type 9 LRVs supplied under the 2014 order operate on Boston's Green Line. Used for the choice of modern articulated Green Line vehicle family; no manufacturer drawing or exact mesh is reproduced.

Search-indexed official presentation describes short-term station accessibility and track work including Blandford. Temporary construction/service changes are intentionally outside this representative campus service.
sources.reviewLimit: Direct PDF fetch returned 403; engineering dimensions were not inferred from it.

geometry.track: Use the unchanged existing median derived between the two MassGIS carriageway axes. Vehicle lane centers at ±1.7325 m match the modeled rail heads at ±1.015 / ±2.45 m (1.435 m gauge). Mobile's adjacent-vertex normals are also used by the vehicle paths; no spline overshoot or relocated roadway.
geometry.vehicle: Authored three-section approximation inspired by Boston's modern articulated green/silver LRVs: 21.7 m car length, 2.64 m width, tapered cabs, chamfered roof, black glazing, sliding doors, three separately aligned bogies and one pantograph. These are bounded model dimensions, not engineering-survey measurements or a manufacturer-accurate Type 9 replica. Two cars carry illustrative fleet numbers 3912 and 3908.
geometry.platformClearance: Existing modern platform center offset 4.1 m was too close for a 2.64 m car. Use shared 4.4 m modern / 4.2 m older offsets, preserving source station anchor/length, so both platform edge and canopy clear the vehicle envelope.
geometry.elevation: Each body section and each bogie independently samples the existing buElevation at its own arc-length position and support endpoints. Rail height remains terrain +0.192 m. No terrain or roadway elevation is changed.
geometry.staticRuntimeDetails: Contact wires, platform back screens/benches, T/B signs and mobile canopies/supports are bounded authored detail. Existing desktop shelters remain. No new collision fences or ground surfaces are introduced.

operation.description: One car per direction; right-hand running. Analytic 0.85 m/s² acceleration/braking, maximum 9 m/s, 13-second stops with platform-side doors. Values are authored for the walking experience, not an MBTA timetable. Each car fades out at the cropped line endpoint before resetting offstage; the model does not invent a loop or reverse the vehicle onto the wrong track.
operation.limits: No boarding, driving, passenger simulation, live arrivals, fare collection, traffic-signal interlocking, moving collision or real closure schedule. Existing pedestrian crossings remain traversable.

runtime.mobile: Dynamic service is excluded from boston.glb. Rigid details are merged per articulated section/material; mobile uses lower wheel segment count, no body shadows and omits decorative side trim. Both directions and all five stop calls are preserved.
runtime.resources: dispose is idempotent and frees owned geometry, materials and CanvasTextures; no texture/network asset download is required.
